title: The zero scheme of the adjoint section
statement:
Let $k$ be a separably closed field,
let $X$ be a smooth projective
curve of
genus $g$ over $k$ with a
$k$-rational point $\sigma$. Let $T$ be
a scheme over $k$ and let
$\mathcal{L}\in F(T)\subseteq\operatorname{Pic}_{X/k,\sigma}(T)$ (with $F$ as in
[lem-pc-f-open-subfunctor]). Let $\mathcal{N}$ be an invertible
$\mathcal{O}_T$-module with $Rf_{T,*}\mathcal{L}\cong\mathcal{N}[0]$, and let $s$ be the section
of $\mathcal{L}\otimes_{\mathcal{O}_{X_T}}f_T^*\mathcal{N}^{-1}$ corresponding to the adjunction
map $f_T^*\mathcal{N}\to\mathcal{L}$ (via
$\operatorname{Hom}(f_T^*\mathcal{N},\mathcal{L})\cong H^0(X_T,\mathcal{L}\otimes f_T^*\mathcal{N}^{-1})$,
the tensor-Hom adjunction, $\mathcal{N}$ invertible). Then the
zero scheme $D:=Z(s)$ is a
relative effective Cartier
divisor on $X_T/T$ which is finite locally free of degree $g$ over $T$.

proof.text:
$\mathcal{M}:=\mathcal{L}\otimes f_T^*\mathcal{N}^{-1}$ is an invertible module on $X_T$ and
$s\in H^0(X_T,\mathcal{M})$. By
[def-pc-zero-scheme] the ideal sheaf
$\mathcal{I}_{Z(s)}=\operatorname{im}(s^\vee)$ is locally generated by one
element, i.e. $D=Z(s)$ is a locally principal closed subscheme ([lem-pc-zero-scheme-properties](1)) of
$X_T$. Also $X_T\to T$ is smooth (base change of the smooth structure
morphism, [lem-pc-proper-base-change]), hence flat
([lem-pc-smooth-flat]), of finite presentation, and of relative
dimension $1$ (fibres are base changes of $X$ by fields, of dimension $1$
by [lem-pc-dim-base-change]).

We verify that every fibre $D_t\subset X_t$ ($t\in T$,
$X_t=X_{\kappa(t)}$) is an effective Cartier divisor on $X_t$; then
$D$ is a relative effective Cartier divisor by [lem-pc-recd-locally-principal],
and the first claim follows.
Let $\kappa=\kappa(t)$ and pass to the fibre: the base change of
$Rf_{T,*}\mathcal{L}\cong\mathcal{N}[0]$ along $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa\to T$ gives
([lem-pc-rf-base-change-flat-module])
$Rf_{\kappa,*}\mathcal{L}_t\cong\mathcal{N}_t[0]$ with $\mathcal{N}_t$ an invertible
$\mathcal{O}_\kappa$-module, i.e. a $1$-dimensional $\kappa$-vector space
$\mathcal{N}_t\cong\kappa$. (The hypotheses of the lemma apply: $X_t\to\operatorname{Spec} \kappa$ is proper of finite presentation and $\mathcal{L}_t$ is finite
presentation and flat over $\kappa$.) Hence
$H^0(X_t,\mathcal{L}_t)\cong\mathcal{N}_t$ and $H^1(X_t,\mathcal{L}_t)=0$ (and
$H^i(X_t,\mathcal{L}_t)=0$ for $i\ge2$ by [lem-pc-vanishing-above-dim],
$\dim X_t=1$; the equality $H^0\cong\mathcal{N}_t$ also uses the canonical
identification of $H^0$ of the complex $\mathcal{N}_t[0]$, [lem-pc-degree-zero-properties]).
In particular $\dim_\kappa H^0(X_t,\mathcal{L}_t)=1$.
Consider the identical analysis for $\mathcal{O}$: $X_t$ is a smooth projective
curve over $\kappa$ with $H^0(X_t,\mathcal{O})=H^0(X,\mathcal{O})\otimes_k\kappa=\kappa$
([lem-pc-flat-base-change-cohom] and
[lem-pc-rational-hyp] plus [prop-pc-xk-integral]) and
$\dim_\kappa H^1(X_t,\mathcal{O})=\dim_\kappa(H^1(X,\mathcal{O})\otimes_k\kappa)=g$
([lem-pc-flat-base-change-cohom], the genus being
$\dim_kH^1(X,\mathcal{O})$, [def-pc-genus]); by
[lem-pc-vanishing-above-dim] the higher cohomology of both vanishes, so [cor-picard-degree-g] applies.
Therefore

$$
\deg(\mathcal{L}_t)=\chi(X_t,\mathcal{L}_t)-\chi(X_t,\mathcal{O}_t)=1-(1-g)=g
$$

([def-pc-degree-line-bundle]; $\chi$ is defined by
[def-pc-euler-characteristic]; the finite-dimensionality and the
finiteness of the sum are [lem-pc-coherent-hi]).
The restriction of the adjunction section to the fibre is the adjoint section for the pulled-back line bundle, by the adjunction base-change statement [lem-pc-zero-scheme-adjunction-base-change].

The section $s_t\in H^0(X_t,\mathcal{M}_t)$ with $\mathcal{M}_t=\mathcal{L}_t\otimes f_t^*\mathcal{N}_t^{-1}$ is non-zero: by the tensor–Hom adjunction in the statement, applied to the fibre data and using the preceding base-change step, it corresponds to the identity of the one-dimensional vector space $\mathcal{N}_t$, so it cannot vanish. By [prop-pc-xk-integral] the fibre $X_t$ is integral. Therefore [lem-pc-nonzero-section-integral-cartier] applies to $s_t$ and shows that its zero scheme $Z(s_t)$ is an effective Cartier divisor. Finally $Z(s_t)$ is the fibre $D_t=D\times_T\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(t)$: the zero scheme of a morphism of invertible modules commutes with pullback along an arbitrary morphism, here $X_t\to X_T$ (which need not be flat) [lem-pc-zero-scheme-pullback], applied to $\mathcal{O}_{X_T}\to\mathcal{M}$, $1\mapsto s$. Hence $D_t$ is an effective Cartier divisor on $X_t$.

Thus $D$ is a relative effective Cartier divisor on $X_T/T$ by
[lem-pc-recd-locally-principal]. Since $X_T\to T$ is smooth of
relative dimension $1$ and proper (base change of proper,
[lem-pc-proper-base-change]), [lem-pc-cartier-criterion] gives
(2)$\Rightarrow$(1): $D\to T$ is finite locally free. For the degree,
[lem-pc-zero-scheme-divisor-iso] applied to the nonzero section on the fibre
gives $\mathcal{O}_{X_t}(D_t)\cong\mathcal{M}_t$. Hence, with $\deg(D_t)=\dim_{\kappa(t)}\Gamma(D_t,\mathcal{O}_{D_t})$ by [lem-pc-degree-base-change](2),
$\deg(D_t)=\deg(\mathcal{M}_t)=\deg(\mathcal{L}_t\otimes f_t^*\mathcal{N}_t^{-1})=\deg(\mathcal{L}_t)=g$.
The last equality uses the computation above and the elementary fact that
$\mathcal{N}_t$ is one-dimensional over $\kappa(t)$, so choosing a basis
identifies $f_t^*\mathcal{N}_t^{-1}$ with $\mathcal{O}_{X_t}$ and leaves degree
unchanged. Since $D\to T$ is finite locally free and the fibre degree at $t$ equals
$\dim_{\kappa(t)}\Gamma(D_t,\mathcal{O}_{D_t})=\deg(D_t)=g$, the morphism
$D\to T$ is finite locally free of degree $g$
([def-pc-finite-locally-free]), as claimed.
